prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2025-12-18. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.71 |
| Retained earnings       | 9,761M |
| Current liabilities     | 18,514M |
| Current assets          | 31,573M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 81,292M |
| Total liabilities       | 89,800M |
| Total assets            | 171,092M |
| EBIT / operating income | 7,508M |
| Revenue                 | 18,015M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2025-12-18, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The provided data indicate a large, capital-intensive firm (low asset turnover) with solid liquidity (current ratio of 1.71), moderate leverage (liabilities at ~52% of assets), strong profitability margins (~42% EBIT), and positive retained earnings. These metrics map to investment-grade credit quality but fall short of the very highest ratings due to the leverage and limited visibility into cash-flow stability or interest coverage.
DECISION: A-
(The data are also consistent with a regulated utility profile, which can sustain this rating despite a low generic Altman Z-score.)
